story_description: As a user, I want to select from available CLI providers when creating a new session, with visual feedback when a CLI is not installed, so that I can quickly understand which providers are available and get guidance on installing missing ones.
task_description: Implement pre-flight validation that checks whether the selected provider CLI binary is installed and accessible on the system PATH before allowing session creation, with clear error states and installation guidance.
atom_description: Create CLIAvailabilityChecker service that detects installed CLIs via which/where commands, caches availability state, and integrates with NewSessionModal to disable unavailable providers and show install prompts.
problem_statement: Users may attempt to create a session with a provider whose CLI is not installed on their system. Without pre-validation, the app would fail at session spawn time with a confusing Process.run error. This atom implements proactive CLI detection to show availability status upfront, disable unavailable providers, and provide a clear path to installation.
scope_in: Implement CLIAvailabilityChecker actor that runs which/where commands to detect CLI binaries
Check for claude, gemini, and codex CLI binaries on system PATH
Cache availability results with configurable TTL to avoid repeated shell calls
Integrate checker with NewSessionModal to query availability on modal open
Disable ProviderCard selection for unavailable CLIs with visual indicator
Show Install button on unavailable provider cards that navigates to onboarding flow
Extract CLI version string when available for display in provider card
Handle edge cases: CLI exists but not executable, CLI exists but returns error on version check
scope_out: Automatic CLI installation - deferred to F005 onboarding flow
Homebrew or package manager integration for installation
Custom CLI path configuration - users must have CLI on standard PATH
Provider-specific authentication validation - separate from CLI availability
Background re-checking while modal is open - single check on open is sufficient
assumptions: Provider CLIs follow standard binary naming: claude for Anthropic, gemini for Google, codex for OpenAI
CLIs are installed in locations included in user PATH environment variable
The which command is available on macOS and returns exit code 0 when binary found
CLIs support a version flag (--version or -v) that returns version string without side effects
NewSessionModal is already implemented with ProviderCard components per atom A003
constraints: Must not block main thread - all shell commands run on background actor
Cache TTL should be short enough to detect installations during app session (30 seconds default)
Must handle PATH not containing expected CLI gracefully without crashes
Shell command timeout must be short (2 seconds max) to avoid hanging modal
Must work with both system-wide and user-local CLI installations (usr/local/bin, ~/.local/bin, etc)
functional_requirements: CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAvailability(provider: EngineType) returns CLIStatus enum with cases: available(version: String), notInstalled, notExecutable, versionCheckFailed
CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAllProviders() returns dictionary mapping EngineType to CLIStatus
NewSessionModal calls checkAllProviders() in onAppear and stores results in local state
ProviderCard receives isAvailable binding and renders disabled state with opacity 0.5 when false
ProviderCard shows Install button overlay when CLI not available, button triggers navigation to onboarding
Selected provider validation prevents Continue button action if selected provider CLI is unavailable
CLI check results are cached in actor-isolated dictionary with timestamp for TTL expiration
Version string displayed in ProviderCard subtitle when CLI is available (e.g. Claude Code v1.2.3)
nonfunctional_requirements: All CLI checks complete within 3 seconds total for all three providers running in parallel
No UI jank or blocking during availability check - modal opens immediately with loading state
Cache reduces shell command overhead for repeated modal opens within TTL window
Graceful degradation if shell commands fail - treat as notInstalled rather than crashing
implementation_steps: Create Blaze/Sources/Services/CLIAvailabilityChecker.swift with actor declaration and CLIStatus enum
Implement private shellCommand helper that runs Process with timeout and captures stdout/stderr
Implement cliPath(for:) method that returns expected binary name for each EngineType
Implement checkAvailability(provider:) that runs which command and parses result
Implement version extraction by running cli --version and parsing first line of output
Add cache dictionary with timestamps and TTL constant, implement cache lookup in checkAvailability
Implement checkAllProviders() that runs all three checks concurrently using TaskGroup
Add @Published availabilityStatus dictionary to NewSessionViewModel or create dedicated state
Wire onAppear in NewSessionModal to call checker and update state
Modify ProviderCard to accept isAvailable and version bindings, implement disabled visual state
Add Install button overlay to ProviderCard that appears when not available
Wire Install button to navigation coordinator to show onboarding CLI installation screen
Add guard in Continue button action to prevent proceeding with unavailable provider
Write unit tests for CLIAvailabilityChecker with mocked Process execution
Write UI test that verifies disabled state renders correctly for unavailable provider
data_model_changes: Add CLIStatus enum: available(version: String), notInstalled, notExecutable, versionCheckFailed
Add CLIAvailabilityCache struct with status: CLIStatus, checkedAt: Date fields
No SQLite schema changes - availability is ephemeral state not persisted to database

CLIAvailabilityChecker.shared singleton access pattern for app-wide usage
event_contracts: No new NormalizedEvent types - CLI availability is pre-session validation
Existing navigation events used for Install button to onboarding flow transition

ui_interactions: User opens New Session modal - triggers availability check for all providers
User sees loading indicators on provider cards during check (brief, sub-second typical)
User sees Install button appear on unavailable provider card
User taps Install button - navigates to onboarding flow for that provider
User taps unavailable provider card - selection prevented, visual feedback via shake or no-op
User selects available provider - normal selection behavior, version shown
User taps Continue with available provider selected - proceeds to session creation
ui_copy: Version check failed subtitle: Unable to verify
Continue button tooltip when disabled: Selected provider CLI is not installed
edge_cases: CLI binary exists but is not executable (chmod issue) - detect via access check and report notExecutable
CLI binary exists but version command fails (corrupted install) - report versionCheckFailed status
PATH environment variable is empty or malformed - handle gracefully, report notInstalled
Multiple CLI versions installed (homebrew and npm global) - which returns first in PATH, use that
CLI installed during app session after initial check - cache TTL allows re-detection on modal reopen
Network-dependent CLI that requires auth before version works (some CLIs) - timeout and report versionCheckFailed
User has alias but not actual binary (alias claude=xyz) - which resolves aliases on macOS, should work
Symlink to CLI that points to missing target - which succeeds but execution fails, detect via test execution
failure_modes: Process.run throws on which command - catch exception, log warning, return notInstalled
Process.run times out (CLI hangs) - terminate process after timeout, return versionCheckFailed
Actor isolation violation - ensure all Process calls happen within actor context
Memory pressure during concurrent checks - TaskGroup handles cancellation gracefully
Modal dismissed during check - Task cancellation propagates, no orphan processes
rollback_plan: Revert CLIAvailabilityChecker.swift and related NewSessionModal changes. ProviderCard returns to always-enabled state. Remove availability check from modal onAppear. Feature gracefully degrades to original behavior where CLI errors surface at session spawn time.

risks: Shell command execution could hang if CLI binary is corrupted or misconfigured
which command behavior may differ on non-standard macOS configurations
Cache TTL too short could cause excessive shell spawning, too long could miss installations
Actor isolation adds complexity and potential for deadlocks if misused
mitigations: Implement strict 2-second timeout on all Process.run calls with SIGKILL fallback
Test on multiple macOS versions and shell configurations during QA
Make cache TTL configurable with sensible default of 30 seconds
Follow Swift actor best practices, avoid blocking calls within actor context
Add comprehensive logging to diagnose any production issues
risk_register.blast_radius: Affects NewSessionModal and ProviderCard UI components. No impact on existing session functionality. Failure degrades to always-available state rather than blocking app usage.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If CLI checking causes issues, disable the feature by having checkAllProviders return all-available. This allows session creation to proceed; CLI errors will surface at spawn time as before.
